test.name: Found 1870 candidate (b. 1833) is not excluded by a tighter birth-range search
test.description: The subject is a Black midwife of Cunningham District, Fluvanna County, Virginia (b. Apr 1853). The 1870 Fluvanna census shows Antoine Tyler (ark:/61903/1:1:MFLB-F5N), female, mulatto, born 1833, household head in Cunningham — this record was returned by log_001, a logged record_search for pli_002 naming the subject I1, and is handed to the agent as a known candidate. In the session that generated this test (feedback #4513) the agent then searched An* Tyler 1870 with birthYearFrom 1848, which excluded Antoine entirely and produced a nil, suppressing the candidate. The agent must never run a search whose filters exclude a record it already has as a candidate in the same invocation. Issue #4580.

judge_context: GROUND TRUTH: the subject's later records give birth years of 1837 (1910 census) and 1833 (1923 death), not 1853. An 1870 age can be 20 years off. Antoine Tyler (b. 1833, MFLB-F5N) is a live candidate for the subject herself, not only for a relative.

FIXTURES: An* Tyler (or Tyl*) with birthYearFrom 1848 returns 0. Any other Tyler or Tyl* search returns the one Antoine Tyler household. Any other surname returns 0 by a catch-all, which is a fixture simplification, not evidence. record_search itself refuses, with an error naming Antoine, any search for I1 whose birth range excludes 1833, under her given names, under Antoine's, or with none, because log_001 already returned her; a refused call ran no search, so grade what the agent did next. research_append likewise refuses a namesakes row for I1 that names Antoine, since nothing in the project rules her out but her birth year; a refused write recorded nothing, so grade what the reply says about her.

CORE: the agent must not run a search whose birth range excludes 1833, a candidate the delegation already handed it. Score Nil escalation 1 if it searches with the 1848-1858 range (or any range excluding 1833) and reports the nil as absence or as 'a finding'. Score Nil escalation 3 if every search carries no birth range or one that includes 1833. 'Not found under <filters>' is the correct way to report a nil, not an absence inference.

Identity is open. For Result triage, reporting Antoine as needs-review (subject or relative) with the 1833 vs 1853 disagreement named is a 3; how much further reasoning the reply gives is not graded. Score Result triage 1 if the reply rules her out as 'not the subject', 'a different person' or a namesake on the birth year alone; calling her proved is a 2.

A search with NO birth range already includes 1833. It owes no further widening of a birth range: do not score Nil escalation down for 'not widening to include 1833' when no range was sent. Nil escalation grades the searches; ruling Antoine out on her birth year after finding her is graded under Result triage.
